ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the traces of compass and straightedge constructions intersect sides $BC$ and $AB$ of $\triangle ABC$ at points D and E, respectively. Construct $DF \perp AB$ at point F. On $AC$, pick a point G such that $DE = DG$. If the area of $\triangle ADG$ is $52$ and the area of $\triangle AED$ is $38$, what is the area of $\triangle DEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct $DH\perp AC$ at H,\\
from the construction traces, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$,\\
$\because$ $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, and $DF\perp AB$, $DH\perp AC$,\\
$\therefore$ $DF=DH$,\\
In right triangles $\triangle DEF$ and $\triangle DGH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}DE=DG\\ DF=DH\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ right $\triangle DEF\cong$ right $\triangle DGH$ (HL),\\
In right triangles $\triangle DAF$ and $\triangle DAH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}DF=DM\\ AD=AD\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ right $\triangle DAF\cong$ right $\triangle DAH$ (HL),\\
$\therefore$ area of $\triangle DEF$ = area of $\triangle DGH$, area of $\triangle DAF$ = area of $\triangle DAH$,\\
$\because$ area of $\triangle ADG$ = area of $\triangle AHD$ + area of $\triangle DGH$, area of $\triangle AHD$ = area of $\triangle ADE$ + area of $\triangle DEF$,\\
$\therefore$ area of $\triangle ADE$ + area of $\triangle DEF$ = area of $\triangle ADG$ - area of $\triangle DGH$,\\
i.e., $38$ + area of $\triangle DEF$ = $52$ - area of $\triangle DEF$,\\
$\therefore$ area of $\triangle DEF$ = $\boxed{7}$,\\

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the construction arcs show AD bisects angle BAC, D is inside the angle on BC, E and F lie on side AB, G lies on side AC, and DF is perpendicular to AB at F. From the text, DE = DG, [AED] = 38, and [ADG] = 52. Draw DH perpendicular to AC. Since D is on the angle bisector, DF = DH; call this common height h. Let x = [DEF]. On side AB, triangles AED and DEF have the same altitude h to line AB, so [ADF] = [AED] + [DEF] = 38 + x. By the equal-distance/angle-bisector setup, right triangles ADF and ADH have common hypotenuse AD and equal leg h, so [ADH] = [ADF] = 38 + x. Therefore [DGH] = [ADG] - [ADH] = 52 - (38 + x) = 14 - x. Now compare right triangles DEF and DGH numerically rather than by full congruence: they have one equal leg DF = DH = h and equal hypotenuses DE = DG. By the Pythagorean theorem, their other legs satisfy EF^2 = DE^2 - h^2 and GH^2 = DG^2 - h^2, so EF = GH. Since their heights to the corresponding side lines are both h, their areas are equal: [DEF] = [DGH]. Thus x = 14 - x, giving x = 7.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, the traces of compass and straightedge constructions intersect sides $BC$ and $AB$ of $\triangle ABC$ at points D and E, respectively. Construct $DF \perp AB$ at point F. On $AC$, pick a point G such that $DE = DG$. If the area of $\triangle ADG$ is $52$ and the area of $\triangle AED$ is $38$, what is the area of $\triangle DEF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct $DH\perp AC$ at H,\\
from the construction traces, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$,\\
$\because$ $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, and $DF\perp AB$, $DH\perp AC$,\\
$\therefore$ $DF=DH$,\\
In right triangles $\triangle DEF$ and $\triangle DGH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}DE=DG\\ DF=DH\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ right $\triangle DEF\cong$ right $\triangle DGH$ (HL),\\
In right triangles $\triangle DAF$ and $\triangle DAH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}DF=DM\\ AD=AD\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ right $\triangle DAF\cong$ right $\triangle DAH$ (HL),\\
$\therefore$ area of $\triangle DEF$ = area of $\triangle DGH$, area of $\triangle DAF$ = area of $\triangle DAH$,\\
$\because$ area of $\triangle ADG$ = area of $\triangle AHD$ + area of $\triangle DGH$, area of $\triangle AHD$ = area of $\triangle ADE$ + area of $\triangle DEF$,\\
$\therefore$ area of $\triangle ADE$ + area of $\triangle DEF$ = area of $\triangle ADG$ - area of $\triangle DGH$,\\
i.e., $38$ + area of $\triangle DEF$ = $52$ - area of $\triangle DEF$,\\
$\therefore$ area of $\triangle DEF$ = $\boxed{7}$,\\

The arc trace in the figure indicates that AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC.
Then reason: Draw DH⊥AC at H. Since D is on the angle bisector, the distances from point D to AB and AC are equal, so DF=DH.
